title: Gravitational Slingshot Launcher
description: A ShaderBall orbits a massive Corset acting as a gravitational anchor in space. The user adjusts orbital velocity, launch angle, gravitational strength, and spin rate, then releases the ShaderBall on a slingshot trajectory through a series of scoring rings. A real-time trajectory preview line updates as parameters change.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a gravitational slingshot physics simulation. Load Corset.glb scaled to 3x and placed at the scene center as a massive gravitational body with a subtle glowing aura (point light inside). Load ShaderBall.glb scaled to 0.8x, initially orbiting the Corset in a circular path. Use OrbitControls for camera, starting at position (0, 5, 15) looking at origin. Add ambient light intensity 0.4 and two directional lights. Create a dark starfield background using a large sphere with star-dot texture or small white spheres. Implement these interactions: (1) A slider for orbital velocity (0.5-5.0, default 2.0) controlling how fast the ShaderBall circles the Corset. (2) A slider for gravitational strength (1-20, default 8) affecting pull force. (3) A slider for launch angle offset (-45 to 45 degrees, default 0) rotating the release direction. (4) A slider for ShaderBall spin rate (0-10 rad/s, default 2) adding visible rotation on release. (5) A 'Preview' button that draws a dashed trajectory line predicting the slingshot path using Euler integration for 200 steps. (6) A 'Launch' button that releases the ShaderBall from its orbit with computed tangential velocity plus angle offset, applying gravitational force each frame via F=GMm/r^2. Place 5 translucent torus rings at computed positions along an ideal trajectory path. When the ShaderBall passes through a ring, the ring turns green and a score counter increments. (7) A 'Reset' button returns the ShaderBall to orbit. Display current velocity magnitude, distance from Corset, and score in an HTML overlay panel. Validate that gravitational strength multiplied by velocity stays below 60 to prevent instability, showing a warning if exceeded. Use requestAnimationFrame with delta time for smooth physics updates.
